description: Three-panel composite of SEM micrographs showing typical inclusion morphologies in LN steel, each panel a single inclusion in a smooth grey matrix with a white halo. (a) a rounded, elongated ellipsoidal grey particle, labelled Mn(Mg)S, with a 2 µm scale bar. (b) a sharply faceted, dark (near-black) diamond/square-shaped particle, labelled AlN, with a 1 µm scale bar; the particle is smaller than those in (a) and (c). (c) a composite duplex inclusion with a 2 µm scale bar: a dark inner core pointed to by an arrow labelled AlN, surrounded by a lighter grey outer shell pointed to by an arrow labelled Mn(Mg)S, so the AlN core is enveloped by Mn(Mg)S. Panel (c) directly links the two single-phase morphologies of (a) and (b) into one particle. No numerical size values are printed beyond the scale bars; inclusion dimensions are therefore read only relative to the 2 µm and 1 µm bars. The figure demonstrates that in LN steel AlN forms as angular, faceted particles and Mn(Mg)S as rounded ones, and that the two can co-precipitate as an AlN-core/Mn(Mg)S-shell composite, supporting the claim that AlN is a dominant inclusion type.

observations.observation: Panel (a) shows an ellipsoidal, rounded grey inclusion labelled Mn(Mg)S with a 2 µm scale bar.
Panel (b) shows an angular, sharply faceted dark inclusion labelled AlN with a 1 µm scale bar.
Panel (c) shows a duplex inclusion in which a dark AlN core is surrounded by a lighter Mn(Mg)S shell, indicated by two labelled arrows.
The Mn(Mg)S inclusions in (a) and (c) are rounded, whereas the AlN inclusion in (b) is faceted and equiaxed, i.e. morphology differs systematically between the two inclusion types.
The scale bar is 1 µm in (b) but 2 µm in (a) and (c), so the AlN particle in (b) is markedly smaller than the inclusions imaged in the other two panels.
No numeric particle-size values are printed in any panel; only scale bars are given.
The caption states the figure presents typical morphologies of inclusions in LN steel.
The citing text asserts that with increasing N content AlN became the dominant inclusion in the current work, consistent with Figure 4-7.
The citing text reports that Alba et al. concluded the main inclusion in Fe-5Mn-3Al steel was an AlN-MnS inclusion for nitrogen contents below 10 ppm.
The paper abstract states AlN is determined to be the main inclusion.
All three panels show the inclusion embedded in a smooth grey matrix with a bright halo at the particle-matrix interface, consistent with a polished metallographic specimen imaged in SEM.

subfigures.description: SEM micrograph of a single rounded, elongated ellipsoidal grey inclusion in a smooth grey matrix, labelled 'Mn(Mg)S'; scale bar 2 µm.
SEM micrograph of a single dark, sharply faceted diamond/square-shaped inclusion, labelled 'AlN'; scale bar 1 µm, indicating a smaller particle than in (a).
SEM micrograph of a duplex inclusion: a dark inner core labelled 'AlN' (arrow) enveloped by a lighter grey outer shell labelled 'Mn(Mg)S' (arrow); scale bar 2 µm.
